response.justification: Broad, deep engineering background (15+ years) with genuine high-throughput distributed systems experience at Sociomantic/dunnhumby (microservices handling millions of HTTP requests/sec, async I/O, fibers, caching) and current Staff-level work at re:cinq building AI-agent infrastructure, MCP code generators, and agentic workflow frameworks — which directly matches the AI-native mindset baseline. Strong TypeScript/Node depth and evident craftsmanship culture (TDD, CI/CD, trunk-based development, teaching/workshops). The main gap is Python, which the JD lists as a must-have and which does not appear anywhere in the skills or work history; the resume is also thin on explicit technical-strategy ownership, cross-functional stakeholder management, and on-call/incident-response evidence expected at Staff level. Worth a screen to probe Python proficiency and scope of influence, but the skills inversion (strong TS, unproven Python) is a real risk.
strengths: Proven high-throughput, low-latency distributed systems at ad-tech scale
Current hands-on AI-agent infrastructure and MCP/agentic tooling work
Deep engineering craftsmanship: TDD, CI/CD, open-source tooling, teaching
concerns: No Python evidence despite it being a must-have skill
Limited demonstrated technical strategy and cross-functional stakeholder leadership
No explicit operational ownership, monitoring, or on-call experience listed

key_factors.factor: AI-agent tooling and agentic workflow exposure
